title: gate-phase-entry.mjs abstains on a tier-restricted row when the tier is undetermined
content: SUPERSEDES the #43-only version of this entry: the sentence 'the 1-ba row's map.json requirement is RETIRED on the mandated path AT EVERY TIER' was TRUE when #43 shipped and is FALSE as of #61 (merged to main as cc41c11, PR #70). Two independent reviewers flagged the stale claim during #61's pipeline; this entry corrects it in place rather than leaving the false sentence to be re-discovered a third time. CURRENT STATE, verified live at origin/main: the `1-ba` row (`plugins/pipeline/scripts/gate-phase-entry.mjs`, `PREREQUISITES["1-ba"]`) is UNCHANGED -- still `{ file: "map.json", tokens: ["0.5"], tiers: ["architectural"] }`, and #43's abstention behaviour still governs it exactly as before (a row carrying a `tiers` key does not apply when `status.risk_tier` is not one of KNOWN_TIERS; `appliesAtTier` reads the RAW field via `tierDetermined`, never `normalizeTier`'s coerced output, so the abstention cannot be silently defeated). What changed is that the map.json obligation is now ALSO enforced at the `2-review` row, via a second key on that row: `also: { file: "map.json", tokens: ["0.5"] }`, checked only after the row's existing `spec.json` + `content: "ba-approved"` primary check passes (re-derive: `git grep -n '"2-review":' -A6 plugins/pipeline/scripts/gate-phase-entry.mjs`). WHY 2-review AND WHY NO TIERS KEY: `2-review` needs no tier restriction of any kind (no `tiers`, no `byTier`) because it is architectural-only BY ROUTING -- `commands/pipeline.md`'s Phase 2 section states 'This phase runs ONLY when spec.risk_tier === "architectural"', re-derive with `git grep -n 'Checkpoint first.*current_phase: "2-review"' plugins/pipeline/commands/pipeline.md` (1 hit) paired with the negative `git grep -c 'Checkpoint first.*current_phase: "1-ba-complete"' plugins/pipeline/commands/pipeline.md` (0 hits, proving the term discriminates a checkpointed entry phase from a pass-through `-complete` literal, not merely a phase name). The published one-hit re-derivation command for the `1-ba` row's own `tiers` key (`git grep -c 'tiers: \[' plugins/pipeline/scripts/gate-phase-entry.mjs` == 1) STILL HOLDS after #61: no second `tiers` key was introduced anywhere, by design (R2/R5 in #61's spec) -- `2-review`'s new obligation is unconditional across all three tier spellings plus the three undetermined spellings, so it needed no tier gate to add. THE `1-ba` row's `tiers` key now does exactly one job: it still polices a REWORK RE-ENTRY (a second visit to `1-ba` with a tier already in the field, per the mechanism explained below); it does nothing on a first visit, which is why the obligation had to be re-sited rather than merely reworded. STORE THE MECHANISM, NEVER THE COUNT -- this is the specific correction #61 asked to be carried forward, because a raw occupancy count decays the moment anyone runs the pipeline again: three independent observers inside #61 alone measured the guarded-row occupancy census at 31, 34, and 43+ distinct committed blob-states within one day, purely because the issue's own checkpoints kept growing the population being counted. What is durable is the MECHANISM and its RE-DERIVATION COMMAND, not any of those numbers. The mechanism: `commands/pipeline.md`'s durable-checkpoint convention makes the exit event for phase N and the entry checkpoint for N+1 ONE write, committed together; the phase-entry guard is invoked from a Stop hook, which can only fire when a turn ENDS at a phase. A `<phase>-complete` literal that the orchestrator writes and then immediately passes THROUGH in that same write, without a turn boundary landing on it, can therefore never be observed as a persisted `current_phase` -- and five of the fifteen guarded rows are exactly that shape (`0.5-map-complete`, `1-ba-complete`, `2-constraints-complete`, `2-review-complete`, `2.5-design-complete`), all `-complete` literals, all with zero occupancy in every census taken so far. The ZEROES are stable under every window and grain measured; the non-zero counts are not, and should never be cited as a fact -- cite the mechanism and this re-derivation command instead: `git log --all --format=%H | while read s; do git ls-tree -r --name-only $s | grep -E '^\.pipeline/[^/]+/status\.json$' | while read f; do echo "$(git rev-parse $s:$f)|$f|$(git show $s:$f | grep -o '\"current_phase\": *\"[^\"]*\"')"; done; done | sort -u`. This is exactly why `1-ba-complete` -- the siting the #61 issue body itself originally proposed -- was REJECTED: it is one of the five never-occupied rows, so a requirement sited there would be unreachable in production however green its tests are; `2-review`, by contrast, is a row runs actually stop at (non-zero occupancy has been observed repeatedly, though per this same rule the count itself is not cited here). HISTORICAL CONTEXT PRESERVED FROM #43 (still true, unaffected by #61): `normalizeTier` still resolves an unusable tier to the strictest row for every ORDINARY tiered check; the `1-ba` row (and, as of #61, no other row) is the deliberate exception, because it is reached at the one checkpoint where the tier is not yet knowable -- BA has not run yet, so `risk_tier` (BA's own output) cannot be relied on there. The guard's own header states the ANCHOR_43 clause byte-identically across the guard comment, `commands/pipeline.md`, and the test's ANCHOR_43 literal: 'the risk_tier at 1-ba is whatever an EARLIER write left there, never the output of the BA dispatch this checkpoint precedes' (re-derive with `git grep -rn 'necessarily absent'` -- note the wording moved on since #43 and this exact phrase is the one that survives; re-check with `git grep -rn 'whatever an EARLIER write left there'` for the current phrasing). A typo'd `risk_tier` still turns a `tiers`-restricted row OFF rather than ON (fail-open on malformed input at that one row, by deliberate analogy to `inFlight`'s treatment of an undated record) -- unaffected by #61, since #61 added no new `tiers` key. #61's own review discipline: 4 review rounds across Phase 2 and Phase 4 (two Phase 4 panel fix rounds, the second triggered by a QA REQUEST_CHANGES on a delta re-review after a fix regraded row shapes by position rather than name only), landing as commit cc41c11 on main (squash of PR #70, base a3f26c1/5b76afd/6ad1b13 in the source branch).
